rules.value: Every successful activation opens a new lifecycle epoch, numbered in increasing order. An epoch pins one generation of the current endpoint instance at a time. The first admitted exchange of an epoch pins that generation, and it must be strictly greater than the generation pinned by any earlier epoch of the same endpoint instance. A later recovery keeps that epoch and does not repeat the activation. It replaces a fenced generation with a successor generation in the same epoch, strictly greater than the fenced generation, and that successor belongs to the same endpoint instance. Admission then requires that successor, so a retry is not left on the fenced generation. A record acquired on the fenced generation is historical and is not current. A record is current only when its epoch, its endpoint instance, and its generation are the live ones. A Restart after an observed activation opens a successor endpoint instance in the same epoch, with empty admission, and enters `ready` on the activation already observed. That Restart sends no echo and does not wait for a second exchange. A Restart before any successful activation enters `activating`, and its driver waits for the documented exchange. An old generation never serves a new epoch.
rules.reason: One successful activation opens the epoch; the pin and record currency are instance-scoped.

rules.value: A retired or replaced endpoint instance refuses every candidate. - The candidate carries the configured endpoint label and the configured node and function FC100. - The candidate carries the transport generation the current epoch pins for the current endpoint instance. For the first exchange of an epoch on that instance, the generation is newer than every earlier epoch of the same endpoint instance. After recovery replaces a fenced generation of that instance, the epoch pins the successor generation of that instance, and a candidate that still carries the replaced generation is refused. A Restart after an observed activation opens a successor endpoint instance in the same epoch, and a candidate that names the replaced instance is refused.
rules.reason: Retired endpoints admit nothing, and generation pins stay on the current endpoint instance.

rules.value: A later recovery does not repeat the activation. Recovery success returns to `ready` with the successor generation pinned in the same epoch. This contract defines no separate cleanup budget: a cancelled or expired acquisition does not start recovery, leaves the endpoint fenced, and leaves the lifecycle `unavailable`. Restart, with its own caller-supplied deadline, is the bounded way back. When the one post-power activation has already been observed, the retained activation report is that observed activation: Restart sends no echo and does not wait for a second exchange, and enters `ready` on the successor endpoint instance. When no activation has been observed, Restart enters `activating` and the driver reports the documented exchange within the activation timeout, or that timeout leaves the lifecycle `unavailable`.
rules.reason: Recovery does not repeat activation; Restart after an observed activation sends no echo.

It is discarded once its age exceeds the retention duration; the last attempt is discarded on the same rule. - A record is current only while the lifecycle is `ready` and its epoch, its endpoint instance, and its generation are the live ones. A record from a fenced generation, another endpoint instance, a replaced endpoint instance, or a closed lifecycle remains historical evidence, may still be fresh by age, and is never current.

rules.section: ## Activation prerequisite and the current NO_SEND gate
rules.value: The lifecycle drives the exchange through an injected activation driver on the endpoint it owns. The driver reports ordered events: the device greeting; the host echo, which is the same bytes as the greeting just received; then either the device confirmation, or a device refusal followed by a new greeting. Readiness requires a report that ends with the confirmation after a host echo of the immediately preceding greeting. A confirmation with no host echo, a refusal, a greeting without a confirmation, an echo that differs from its greeting, any other bytes, or any other order never admits readiness. The tokens are `TESLA`, `PASS` and `FAIL`, each followed by NUL, compared exactly. The activation deadline is taken from the lifecycle clock before the driver is called.
rules.reason: Readiness requires the confirmation after a host echo of the immediately preceding greeting, and the deadline is sampled first.

These are host-side values, not wire timing. This page publishes no measured duration or count for that report.
rules.reason: The activation report keeps host-side offsets and echo intervals and publishes no measured number.

rules.section: ## Activation prerequisite and the current NO_SEND gate
rules.value: An optional readiness probe is an explicitly configured use of the first configured read operation. It applies only when the driver reports silence for the whole activation timeout, meaning no event at all. An acknowledged result opens the epoch. Any other result leaves the lifecycle `unavailable`. It is never used after any event was reported. It is a transmission and it is off unless configured.
rules.reason: The readiness probe is an explicit transmission used only after silence.

rules.section: ## Activation prerequisite and the current NO_SEND gate
rules.value: The only bytes the lifecycle causes to be transmitted are the planned read requests, the one provisional current-limit mutation, and the host echo of a greeting. The echo is sent only by a driver whose configuration selects the responder explicitly. A Restart after an observed activation sends no echo and does not wait for a second exchange.
rules.reason: The lifecycle transmits planned reads, the one provisional mutation, and an explicitly selected host echo.

rules.value: The version label has the form `wc3_` followed by three underscore-separated integers. Builds of one line share the first two integers, so the read line is `wc3_24_44`, and the third integer orders builds of that line. The read floor is the identified, capability-compatible label `wc3_24_44_3`: a build on that line whose third integer is at least 3, and whose activation, private-function, and operation capabilities are compatible. An unidentified build, including an ambiguous or missing version and a build that is not on the `wc3_24_44` line, is refused with that reason and nothing is sent. A build on that line whose third integer is below 3 is refused as below-floor and nothing is sent. A build whose activation, private function, or operation schema is incompatible is refused as capability-incompatible and nothing is sent. The level stays `not_tested_on_hardware` unless an operator-owned public observation records `tested_on_hardware`, and neither level conditions admission. The independently qualified provisional current-limit mutation stays bound to the exact operation version `wc3_24_44_3`.
rules.reason: Read admission uses one identified, capability-compatible floor and names the three refusals.

rules.value: The read floor is the identified, capability-compatible label `wc3_24_44_3` on the `wc3_24_44` line. A `compatible_candidate` is admitted for these reads only when it is identified on that line at or above the floor and those capabilities are compatible. An unidentified build, including an ambiguous or missing version and a build that is not on the `wc3_24_44` line, is refused with that reason and nothing is sent. A build on that line whose third integer is below 3 is refused as below-floor and nothing is sent. rules.reason: Admission admits an identified build at or above the read floor and refuses the other three cases.
